exampleDetails: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)

crawl.consoleErrorNote: The single console error is the browser reporting the F-005 transient document 404 ("Failed to load resource"); it is not an application exception.

findings.symptom: Documented public probes were answered by Apache with the SPA index.html (HTTP 200, text/html) instead of the backend response.
findings.expected: Backend JSON, as documented in docs/PRODUCTION_RUNBOOK.md section 4.
findings.actual: Any monitoring, load-balancer or operator probe of /healthz or /readyz received a 200 HTML page and could never detect a backend or database outage.
findings.rootCause: public/.htaccess (the build source copied to dist/.htaccess) proxied only ^api/ to the backend. The documented public probe paths fell through to the SPA catch-all RewriteRule ^ index.html.
findings.fix: Added a RewriteRule for ^(healthz|readyz|llms\.txt|public/.*\.json)$ using the [P] proxy flag directly to 127.0.0.1:8080.
findings.regressionTest: crawl-artifacts/harness/validate-subsystems.mjs (16/16 pass); live /healthz returns application/json with authoritativeDatabase=MARIADB.
findings.notes: The [P] flag is required because the VirtualHost ProxyPass /api is evaluated before .htaccess rewriting; an api/index.php target is re-proxied to the backend as /api/index.php and never reaches PHP (that variant returned 401 during validation).

findings.symptom: The contact page had no h1 landmark; its primary heading was rendered as an h2.
findings.expected: Exactly one h1 per page for the document heading.
findings.actual: Crawler reported NO_H1 on /contact at every viewport.
findings.rootCause: src/components/Contact/Contact.jsx line 156 used <h2> for the page title.
findings.fix: Promoted the page heading to <h1>; Tailwind classes unchanged so rendering is identical.
findings.regressionTest: Crawl reports zero NO_H1 findings; live DOM returns h1 = "Get in Touch".

findings.symptom: A single homepage render issued 10 identical public-config requests (~10 redundant MariaDB reads, ~53 KB duplicate transfer).
findings.expected: One read shared by every consumer of the authoritative projection.
findings.actual: Navbar, footer, language picker, templates, pricing, analytics and meta manager each fetched independently.
findings.rootCause: src/services/api/platform.js had no shared in-flight promise or short-lived cache for the public projection.
findings.fix: Added fetchPublicConfig() with in-flight coalescing and a 15s snapshot, mirroring the existing backend patterns in featureFlagService.js and platformHealth.js. Failures are never cached; the snapshot is invalidated only on admin writes.
findings.regressionTest: Measured 10 -> 3 requests with byte-identical rendered content (11482 vs 11481 chars) and zero console errors; 511 product tests pass.

findings.symptom: Horizontal page scroll on mobile: document scrollWidth 492 vs clientWidth 430.
findings.rootCause: The CTA section background wrapper in src/components/Features/Features.jsx lacked overflow-hidden, so a decorative w-96 blur orb offset by left-1/4 extended past the viewport. The sibling wrapper at line 257 already had overflow-hidden.
findings.fix: Added overflow-hidden to the background wrapper, matching the sibling pattern.
findings.regressionTest: scrollWidth == clientWidth verified at 360, 375, 390, 430, 768, 1024 and 1440; the post-fix crawl reports zero H_OVERFLOW findings.

findings.symptom: Rare, non-deterministic 404 on the document request itself during long crawls (7 occurrences in 20,000 sampled requests = 0.035%).
findings.expected: Every SPA route consistently returns 200 from the rewrite fallback.
findings.actual: One crawl of 539 visits hit a single such 404; the pre-fix crawl hit a different route with the same signature.
findings.reproduction: Not reproducible in isolation: 0/10 single-route attempts, 0/12 under 12-way parallel load, and 50/50 rapid curl requests all returned 200.
findings.rootCause: Transient Apache/mod_rewrite behaviour on Windows under sustained load. The failing request is the document request recorded as 404 in the Apache access log; application code, the Express backend and MariaDB are not involved.
findings.fix: No application change made. The evidence does not implicate the application, and no speculative change was introduced.
findings.regressionTest: Apache access log shows 7 404s and 0 5xx across the last 20,000 requests.
